newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - U.S. ADRs boosted by economic data.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - U.S. ADRs boosted by economic data.

text.p: Foreign stocks followed U.S. markets higher on Friday, helped by economic data pointing to low American inflation, analysts said.

The Labor Department reported consumer prices rose only 0.1 percent in August. The inflation figure eased fears the Federal Reserve might raise interest rates and the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped to record territory on the news.
Among American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), Sweden's LM Ericsson telecommunications company flirted with a year's high, rising by midday to 25-1/8, up 3/4, on trade of 3.3 million shares.

Ericsson was helped by a Cowen & Co recommendation that raised the company to buy from neutral and from general interest in technology stocks that pushed up the Nasdaq Composite Index 19 percent at midday.
"Ericsson has really had a real nice move," an analyst said. "Obviously with the CPI numbers the whole market is up."
Interest-sensitive Latin American stocks were up also as the yield on U.S. Treasury's 30-year bond fell to below seven percent, making the shares more attractive.

Argentine oil company YPF rose 5/8 to 23-1/2, also near a year high, on general interest in oil stocks because of tension over Iraq. Investors also "see a better tone in Argentina generally" despite the Argentine Congressional delay in voting on a fiscal package, one analyst said.
Brazilian state telephone company Telebras rose to 78-5/8, up 1-5/8, helped by recent financial presentations in the United States by company executives.

Investors also are waiting for a decision from the U.S. government on whether to lift or reduce a tariff on Mexican cement. A reduction or elimination would help stocks of Mexican cement company Cemex SA.
